case_study_insert.main_stem: Millgrove Grain Kitchens (MGK) is a sole trader in the cereal and grain-milling sector, employing a workforce of 55. Founded in 2003 by Owen Millgrove, it supplies breakfast cereals to regional food retailers and operates a hierarchical structure with democratic leadership. MGK plans to invest $840,000 in a new grain mill and packaging line, financed by a $520,000 ten-year bank loan and $320,000 of retained profit. It has fixed costs of $300,000 a year, a variable cost of $6.25 a unit and a selling price of $12.25, and currently produces 75,000 units a year for its regional retail customers. MGK faces two problems: waste of 4.6% and absenteeism of 7%.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Waste and Market Report — Q3 2025: The mill packed 18,750 units last quarter at a waste rate of 4.6%, down from 6.0% a year ago. Customer complaints fell from 37 to 20 a month. Average delivery time is 3.1 days. A survey of 650 shoppers found that 70% would pay up to $0.40 more for wholegrain cereals and 54% check fibre content before buying. Training records show 14 of 55 staff have not completed on-the-job training on the new packaging line; off-the-job training courses at the local college cost $850 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Millgrove Grain Kitchens as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.4% to 5.15%, lifting borrowing costs on variable-rate loans. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 6.0% from $13.10 to $13.89 an hour from April 2026, increasing wage bills. (3) Wheat and packaging input costs have risen 12.0% year-on-year, food-price inflation is 7.0% and consumer spending on breakfast cereals grew 3.0% in the same period.

questions.question_text: MGK plans to fund part of its mill expansion with a ten-year bank loan. Explain two advantages for MGK of using retained profit instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit of $320,000 requires no interest or instalments, so the sole trader avoids piling debt service on fixed costs of $300,000 a year while already owing $520,000 to the bank. The cash saved can attack the 4.6% waste rate and protect the $6.00 contribution earned on each of 75,000 cereal units, improving the return on the $840,000 mill investment.

Point 2: Internal funding keeps ownership and decisions with founder Owen Millgrove and avoids bank covenants or security over the new mill. If the 7% absence rate held back output, a lender might demand repayment, whereas retained profit carries no such threat. Because MGK has democratic leadership in a hierarchical structure, the owner can consult staff on how to use the $320,000 immediately for the 14 of 55 workers needing training, while leaving the $520,000 loan available for seasonal working capital rather than increasing borrowing.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of retained profit over a bank loan (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to MGK's $320,000 retained profit, loan, waste and staffing.

questions.question_text: MGK is launching its new wholegrain cereal range. Consider a national television campaign, local radio sponsorship, or social media influencer marketing. Which should MGK choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
National television campaign: Television could build quick, mass awareness of wholegrain cereals across all regional retailers. The cost is high and a substantial share of viewers buys no cereal or lives outside the delivery area, so much of the spend is wasted. For a 55-worker sole trader with $300,000 fixed costs and a $520,000 loan, that money is better spent reducing 4.6% waste and supporting the $840,000 mill than on expensive airtime.

Local radio sponsorship: Regional radio is cheap and reaches MGK's local catchment with a short launch message. Its reach is limited relative to the 75,000-unit output and the regional retailer network, and radio cannot show the wholegrain product or fibre message as clearly as visual media, so it cannot drive the required volume alone.

Social media influencer marketing: Influencers can demonstrate fibre benefits to the 70% of 650 surveyed shoppers willing to pay $0.40 more and the 54% checking fibre content, with precise targeting, national reach and measurable engagement at modest cost. Results build slowly and rely on credibility, but the fit with survey evidence is the closest.

Recommendation: MGK should choose social media influencer marketing. It reaches the identified shoppers nationally, costs far less than television and supports the premium behind the $6.00 contribution per unit. Television is rejected as costly and wasteful; radio is rejected because it cannot deliver enough reach for regional retailer listings.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies promotional options with limited MGK context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in MGK's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options and recommends influencer marketing, explaining why television and radio are rejected.

questions.question_text: MGK's waste is 4.6% and absenteeism is 7%. Explain two benefits for MGK of using job rotation to motivate its production team.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Job rotation moves the 55 workers between milling and packing tasks, reducing repetition and boredom and encouraging staff to spot waste at each stage. That can lower the 4.6% waste rate and protect the $6.00 contribution on 75,000 units, making better use of the $840,000 mill without extra capital. Staff who understand several processes can cover for absent colleagues, limiting disruption from the 7% absence rate.

Point 2: Rotation develops a more versatile workforce and raises morale because employees gain new skills and variety, which supports MGK's democratic leadership. Higher motivation can reduce absence and the need to retrain the 14 of 55 staff still needing on-the-job training, where college courses cost $850 each. A flexible team also helps the sole trader meet retailer orders consistently while the new packaging line beds in.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of job rotation (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to MGK's 4.6% waste, 7% absence and training needs.

questions.question_text: MGK must upskill 14 staff to operate the new packaging line. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the local college. Which should MGK choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Coaching at the packaging line suits MGK's own machines and cereal standards, costs no fees and keeps the 14 trainees productive while learning, protecting the 18,750 units packed last quarter and the drop in waste from 6.0% to 4.6%. The drawbacks are that mentors are production workers whose work suffers, errors could add to the 4.6% waste, and no certificate is provided that retailers might value.

Off-the-job training: The college course at $850 per employee totals $11,900 for 14 staff, small against the $840,000 investment, and offers structured teaching with a recognised qualification. It takes 14 of 55 workers away from the line, reducing capacity and possibly aggravating 7% absence, and generic content may not match MGK's exact packaging settings without follow-up.

Decision: MGK should choose on-the-job training first, adding short college modules for senior operators later. It is machine-specific, avoids $11,900 in fees and protects the 18,750-unit quarterly pack while waste stands at 4.6%. Full off-the-job training is rejected because losing 14 of 55 staff would slow deliveries to regional retailers and the generic course cannot replace plant-specific practice; certification can be added once the line is stable.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Describes the two training methods with limited MGK context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses benefits and drawbacks of one or both methods in MGK's context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates both methods in context with a justified decision on cost, disruption and machine relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how MGK's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.
questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 50,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $6.00 | (iii) Four applied uses: margin of safety of 25,000 units; average total cost of $10.25; labour productivity of about 1,364 units per worker; servicing the $520,000 loan.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $300,000 ÷ ($12.25 − $6.25) = $300,000 ÷ $6.00 = 50,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 50,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $12.25 − $6.25 = $6.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $6.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways MGK's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Break-even of 50,000 units against output of 75,000 units gives a margin of safety of 25,000 units, showing the buffer against 4.6% waste.
2. Average total cost of $300,000 ÷ 75,000 + $6.25 = $10.25 a unit benchmarks milling and packing efficiency.
3. Labour productivity of 75,000 units ÷ 55 staff = about 1,364 units a worker tests whether 7% absence is sustainable.
4. Contribution of $6.00 sets the volume needed to service the $520,000 bank loan for the $840,000 mill.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate MGK's liquidity by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has MGK's liquidity improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.32 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.51 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 0.61 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 0.88 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $140,000 inventories + $85,000 trade receivables + $33,000 cash = $258,000; 2025 current assets = $118,000 + $104,000 + $58,000 = $280,000. Dividing by $195,000 and $185,000 current liabilities gives 1.32 and 1.51. Excluding inventories: 2024 = ($258,000 − $140,000) ÷ $195,000 = 0.61; 2025 = ($280,000 − $118,000) ÷ $185,000 = 0.88.

Evaluation: Both measures improved. The current ratio rose from 1.32 to 1.51 as current assets grew by $22,000 and current liabilities fell by $10,000, giving a better cushion for paying suppliers while the sole trader services a $520,000 loan. The acid test rising from 0.61 to 0.88 is the stronger evidence of genuine improvement because it excludes inventories, which for cereal with 4.6% waste may not convert easily to cash. Cash rose from $33,000 to $58,000, improving day-to-day flexibility. The concern is that trade receivables increased from $85,000 to $104,000 with regional retailers, tying up cash, and the acid test remains below 1, so MGK still depends partly on stock to pay current debts.

Conclusion: MGK's liquidity has improved, with both ratios higher and the gain not driven by building inventory. Nevertheless, an acid test of 0.88 and rising receivables mean the owner should tighten credit control before committing further funds to the $840,000 mill.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures with little accurate ratio calculation.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Calculates both ratios for both years accurately with contextual comment on the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratios, evaluation of inventory, receivables, cash and liabilities, and a justified conclusion.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for MGK of promoting its cereals as wholegrain.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Of 650 shoppers surveyed, 70% would pay up to $0.40 more for wholegrain cereals and 54% check fibre content. That supports a price above $12.25 and protects the $6.00 contribution per unit against 12.0% wheat and packaging inflation, while helping sell 75,000 units to regional retailers and justifying the $840,000 mill investment.

Disadvantage: Wholegrain ingredients and clearer labelling may raise the $6.25 variable cost per unit, but the insert does not decompose that cost, so the exact increase cannot be stated; if the $0.40 premium is not accepted across the range, contribution falls. There is also a risk that if fibre claims disappoint the 54% who check labels, demand could weaken while MGK still has 4.6% waste and 7% absence, and the $520,000 loan requires cash whatever happens.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development using MGK's survey data and cost structure.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.15%, the 6.0% minimum wage increase and the 12.0% rise in wheat and packaging input costs will affect MGK. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.4% to 5.15%): If the $520,000 ten-year loan is variable-rate, the added annual cost is 0.75% × $520,000 = $3,900 (0.0075 × $520,000), modest against $300,000 fixed costs and zero if the rate is fixed. The rise may also make consumers more cautious and future borrowing dearer, but MGK can limit this by fixing the rate.

Minimum wage increase (6.0%, to $13.89 an hour): With 55 workers this feeds into the wage bill and cannot be refused. The insert provides no hours or individual pay, so an annual wage total cannot legitimately be invented. The defensible test is productivity: 75,000 units ÷ 55 staff = about 1,364 units per worker, so the rise is manageable only if that productivity holds or output grows; otherwise unit labour cost erodes the $6.00 contribution.

Input-cost inflation (12.0% wheat and packaging): The $6.25 variable cost is not broken down, so only a bound is honest: if all of it rose 12.0%, that is $0.75 a unit (0.12 × $6.25), about $56,250 a year at 75,000 units. Even partial pass-through cuts contribution, though the $0.40 wholegrain premium and 3.0% demand growth can soften the effect.

Conclusion: The 12.0% rise in wheat and packaging costs will have the greatest impact because it applies to every one of the 75,000 units and directly reduces the $6.00 contribution underpinning the $840,000 mill. The interest effect is a known $3,900, and the wage effect rests on unstated hours, whereas input inflation is broad and persistent and cannot be removed by a single adjustment.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited MGK application.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on MGK's costs and finance in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three changes and concludes input-cost inflation has the greatest impact with reasons.
